query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: staff_attitude
per_column.rationale: A text-derived characterization of staff behaviour (warm/indifferent/rude/professional). This is an experiential driver antecedent to the overall rating, not a restatement of it. It plausibly carries strong predictive signal for satisfaction and is not deterministically implied by the rating itself, so it is a legitimate feature (partially overlapping the existing Staff Service score but adding qualitative nuance).

per_column.name: service_consistency_pattern
per_column.rationale: Describes whether service was consistently high/poor, mixed, or declining. This is a service-quality attribute, a driver of satisfaction rather than a synonym for it. The valence embedded (consistently_high vs consistently_poor) makes it correlated with the outcome, but it still refers to a specific aspect (service consistency) that lies outside the focus, so it qualifies as a predictor, albeit a valence-heavy and somewhat redundant one.

per_column.name: food_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: Aspect-level assessment of food/meal experience (excellent/adequate/poor/failure). This is a distinct dimension of the trip experience that drives, but does not restate, overall satisfaction. Legitimate predictor (overlaps the existing Food & Beverages rating but adds failure-mode granularity).

per_column.name: hard_product_condition
per_column.rationale: Physical condition of the seat/cabin (new_clean/worn_dated/broken_faulty). An objective-ish attribute of the product experienced, external to the rating and plausibly predictive of it. Legitimate feature.

per_column.name: flight_disruption_type
per_column.rationale: Objective operational event (delay/cancellation/missed connection/overbooking/none). This is an exogenous antecedent event, clearly outside the focus and not captured by any original numeric aspect rating, so it provides genuinely new and strong predictive signal for satisfaction.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: How any disruption was handled (proactive/adequate/poor/NA). A recovery-experience driver that lies outside the overall rating and adds signal not present in the original ratings. Valenced but aspect-specific, so a legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: overbooking_seat_assignment_issue
per_column.rationale: Boolean flag for an objective adverse event. Exogenous to the rating, not a restatement, and plausibly predictive of dissatisfaction. Legitimate feature (partially redundant with the overbooking category in flight_disruption_type).

per_column.name: customer_service_resolution_quality
per_column.rationale: Quality/outcome of interacting with customer service (unresolved, rude, resolved, etc.). A service-recovery driver that is distinct from the overall rating and not present in original columns, so it adds predictive signal. Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: value_perception
per_column.rationale: poor/fair/good_value is a global evaluative judgment that is nearly synonymous with overall satisfaction and directly duplicates the existing 'Value For Money' column. It is a summary valence judgment rather than an independent driver, so it largely restates/leaks the focus and offers little exogenous predictive leverage.

judge.rationale: The set is semantically rich rather than mechanical: it consists mostly of aspect-level experiential drivers and objective operational events extracted from review text. The disruption-related and service-recovery features (flight_disruption_type, disruption_handling_quality, overbooking_seat_assignment_issue, customer_service_resolution_quality) are the strongest contributors because they are exogenous events not represented in the original numeric ratings, providing genuinely additive signal for predicting overall rating. The qualitative aspect descriptors (staff_attitude, food_quality_signal, hard_product_condition, service_consistency_pattern) are legitimate predictors but overlap substantially with the existing Staff Service / Food & Beverages / Seat Comfort ratings, reducing their marginal lift. value_perception is a near-synonym of overall satisfaction and duplicates Value For Money, so it is treated as a restatement/leakage rather than an independent predictor. Overall, 8 of 9 columns are valid predictors with meaningful but partly redundant marginal value beyond the original columns.
